The check is `isProjectPath` in `src/core/manifest.ts` (line 42-46).

It's invoked from `readManifest` (same file, line 66), which filters out any manifest entry whose `path` is not a safe project-relative path before that list is ever handed to `sync()`'s deletion loop.

How it works: `isProjectPath(cwd, p)` rejects the entry if `p` is absolute (`path.isAbsolute(p)`) or looks like a Windows drive path (`/^[a-zA-Z]:/`), and otherwise resolves `p` against `cwd` and checks that the resulting relative path doesn't start with `..` (i.e., doesn't escape `cwd`). So even if `.agentos/manifest.json` is hand-edited to contain `../secret.txt` or `C:\secret.txt`, `readManifest` silently drops that entry — `sync()` (`src/commands/sync.ts:106-141`) only ever calls `rmSync` on entries that survived this filter, so the malicious entry never reaches the deletion loop.
